nodes.label: Bakeoff Harness & Logging Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Tasks 1-12 building the instrumented run harness. Scoring is deliberately absent -- this plan produces the raw record that later plans derive scores from. Every module owns one responsibility and is testable without Docker except container, claude_runner and runner.

nodes.label: Task 1: Schema and append-only event log
nodes.rationale: Records open with mode 'x' so overwriting is impossible; the index is appended only after the record is fsynced and atomically renamed, so the index never advertises a run that does not exist. No update or delete API exists anywhere in the package -- excluded runs keep their records.

nodes.label: Task 2: Cost calculation and PRICE_BOOK
nodes.rationale: Candidate cache multipliers are explicitly None rather than guessed: AWS publishes no cache pricing for any of the three, and guessing would silently corrupt the headline cost metric, so observed cache tokens raise instead.

nodes.label: Price correction 2026-08-05: Kimi output $3.00 not $2.50
nodes.rationale: The plan doc had taken the optimistic end of Model_Bakeoff_Plan.md's '$2.50-3.00' range; re-verifying all four against the AWS pricing page corrected it, along with the 3.10 -> 3.60 test expectation.

nodes.label: Task 3: Tolerant trajectory parser
nodes.rationale: Parsing is deliberately tolerant: a run killed mid-write leaves a partial final line, and losing the whole trajectory over one truncated line would violate the spec's no-data-loss requirement. Malformed lines are counted, not swallowed.

nodes.label: Timing correction: inference_ms vs tool_exec_ms must partition the span
nodes.rationale: Measuring inference as the gap between consecutive assistant records folds tool execution into it and leaves tool_exec_ms permanently zero -- against the fixture that left 5s of 30s unaccounted. A split that cannot distinguish a slow model from a slow test run makes the latency success criterion unusable. Tool-result records carry timestamps, so the real split is already in the transcript.

nodes.label: Task 4: Destructive-command and secret scanners
nodes.rationale: reverted_by_agent and affected_outcome are hardcoded False, so severity is permanently HIGH and OPEN-10's MEDIUM tier is unreachable at scan time. Revert detection needs checkpoint file state; inferring it from the bash stream alone would miss Write-tool restores and produce false MEDIUM downgrades, so conservative HIGH is the right default and a test pins the unresolved status.

nodes.label: Task 5: Container lifecycle and git pinning
nodes.rationale: Digest-pinned image, detached checkout, snapshot_diff and restore_paths. Every git call routes through _checked_exec because a failed `git diff` returns empty output byte-identical to a clean tree. The digest check accepts a bare sha256: image id since a locally built image has no registry digest.

nodes.label: macOS bind-mount hazard (empty mount reads as clean tree)
nodes.rationale: The Docker VM mounts $HOME but not /var/folders where pytest's tmp_path lives, so the repo mounts as an empty directory with no error and git's 'not a git repository' goes to stderr. Snapshot tests then compare nothing against nothing and pass. Fixed by --basetemp under $HOME plus direct mount and git-availability assertions.

nodes.label: Task 6: Live checkpoint capture
nodes.rationale: Capture happens on stdout turn boundaries while the agent works, so staging must go to a throwaway GIT_INDEX_FILE -- staging under a live agent means a later agent commit sweeps in files it never staged and its git status disagrees with reality. Boundary precision is approximate by however long a snapshot takes, recorded rather than hidden.

nodes.label: Checkpoint off-by-one: report turns completed, not announced
nodes.rationale: An assistant message announces the tool calls a turn is about to make, so at message k the tree still holds k-1 turns of work. Firing on_turn(k) there files turn k-1's work under turn k and understates every checkpoint by one -- on the exact axis the cost-at-budget-K curve is plotted against.

nodes.label: Task 7: Wire-level logging and litellm config
nodes.rationale: Both transports are configured so Phase 0 can pick per arm from evidence and an adapter failure can be told apart from model weakness. Every model_name is distinct on purpose -- LiteLLM round-robins repeated names, which would randomize transport per call and confound latency and tool-translation results -- and model_name doubles as the PRICE_BOOK key.

nodes.label: LiteLLM callbacks must be CustomLogger instances
nodes.rationale: success_handler dispatches on isinstance(callback, CustomLogger), so a duck-typed object is skipped in silence -- no wire log, no error, against a mandatory requirement. Worse, get_instance_fn resolves a dotted path with getattr and returns it as-is, so a path to a class lands the class object in the callback list and fails the same check. The fix is a dotted path to a module-level instance.

nodes.label: Task 8: Failure and exclusion classification
nodes.rationale: Produces RunSignals, classify_failure, classify_exclusion and a pre-registered reason-code set, per the spec's requirement that exclusion criteria are written down before the run begins.

nodes.label: FALSE_SUCCESS correction: tests_passed is None, not False
nodes.rationale: With tests_passed hardcoded False, the normal healthy path -- agent finishes, no malformation, no truncation, no loop -- reached `agent_claimed_success and not tests_passed` and stamped FALSE_SUCCESS, an accusation of dishonesty, on every clean run. Grading is offline, so the harness must not pre-judge: None means unknown.

nodes.label: Task 9: Claude Code runner and config isolation
nodes.rationale: Builds the command, env and config_digest against claude 2.1.220. --max-turns exists but is hidden from --help, verified by inspecting the binary rather than assumed.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, not --settings, detaches user config
nodes.rationale: --settings loads ADDITIONAL settings on top of ~/.claude/settings.json, and --strict-mcp-config covers MCP servers only -- leaving hooks, skills, output styles, plugins and user CLAUDE.md in place. The plan had also stripped CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, which makes the CLI fall back to ~/.claude: the lever pulled the wrong way. Setting it to an empty per-run directory relocates all of it at once.

nodes.label: Environment is an allowlist, not a denylist
nodes.rationale: A denylist over the inherited env missed the load-bearing case: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK and _USE_VERTEX make the CLI ignore ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, bypass the proxy and leave the mandatory wire log empty while the run looks normal. An allowlist fails closed.

nodes.label: Per-run transcript discovery
nodes.rationale: Returning the newest *.jsonl in the project dir lets a run that crashes before writing inherit the previous model's trajectory, tokens and cost. The munging rule was also wrong -- Claude Code hyphenates dots as well as separators -- so any repo path with a dot resolved to a nonexistent directory and recorded zeros without complaint. Both close by globbing the per-run config dir.

nodes.label: Temperature is per-model and excluded from config_digest
nodes.rationale: A single uniform temperature would 400 every call on the reference arm (Sonnet 5 rejects non-default sampling) and convert Kimi's documented temperature-0 stall into a latency measurement. Folding a necessarily-per-model value into a cross-arm identity digest would make the digest assert something false.

nodes.label: Task 10: Run orchestrator (execute_run)
nodes.rationale: Composes Tasks 1-9 into one run producing exactly one record. Closing its eleven carried-forward defects changed the architecture twice: the agent moved inside the container, and checkpoints moved to live capture.

nodes.label: Internal Docker network with the proxy as a peer
nodes.rationale: 'Agent in the container' and network_mode=none were mutually exclusive; §5.1's 'or through a recording proxy' branch resolves it. An internal=True network has no host route, so 127.0.0.1:4000 is unreachable by design and the proxy must run as a container on that network. Asserting only that the internet is blocked would pass on a container with no network at all -- the one configuration the agent cannot work under.

nodes.label: Defect 12: api_error_status never populated
nodes.rationale: execute_run never passed it to assemble_record, so the throttle/5xx exclusion branch was unreachable and every Bedrock 429 was scored against the model. The drafted test called classify_exclusion directly and passed green over the dead path. Now derived from the wire log, counting only the last call and only if it failed.

nodes.label: Defect 13: version block 4/6 empty on every record
nodes.rationale: litellm, bedrock_model_id, harness_commit and task_set_commit were empty strings on every record written. Now from importlib.metadata (litellm.__version__ does not exist in 1.95.0 and raises AttributeError), git rev-parse with a -dirty suffix, and the resolved model read off the wire.

nodes.label: Defect 14: checkpoints discarded on mid-run failure
nodes.rationale: `checkpoints = recorder.captured` sat inside the try, so any mid-run failure threw away every checkpoint already captured and the record still looked well-formed -- an empty checkpoint list is indistinguishable from a quiet run. The recorder is now held outside the try and read in the finally.

nodes.label: Defect 15: wire capture registered in the wrong process
nodes.rationale: Callbacks registered in the harness process, which makes no LLM calls -- the agent runs in its own container and the model call is made by the proxy, a third process. Every real run would have produced an empty wire log and with it empty sampling and hashes, silently. Closed by moving capture into the proxy and replaying those lines through the existing WireLogger so there is still one canonical artifact.

nodes.label: Task 11: Fault-injection gate (verify_logger.py)
nodes.rationale: With no Docker daemon the gate returns GATE INCOMPLETE and exit 1, not a pass: half of §6.6 is only observable against a real daemon, and reporting 'passed' on the strength of checks that cannot see those is the exact failure the gate exists to prevent. Includes a negative control so the positive capture test cannot pass on in-process capture.

nodes.label: Task 12: End-to-end smoke test (Phase 0c)
nodes.rationale: Offline half done 2026-08-06: real Claude Code binary, pinned container, real proxy on an internal network, real streaming SSE from a stub -- 3 turns, 2 tool calls, a 157-byte staged diff, zero unattributed calls. Building it turned up four more defects none of the existing tests could see.

nodes.label: Defect 16: production proxy config registered no wire callback
nodes.rationale: Defect 15 in a second place: every real run would have read an empty wire directory. The config comment argued correctly about a dotted path to a class; the fix is a path to a module-level instance.

nodes.label: Defect 17: eval_settings.json was mounted nowhere
nodes.rationale: --settings named a path no image had, and Claude Code does not fail on a missing settings file -- it starts with none of the pinned settings, the agent cannot edit anything, and a one-line harness omission reads as four capability findings.

nodes.label: Defect 18: the image ran as root
nodes.rationale: Claude Code refuses bypassPermissions under root and --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions does not lift the guard. Visible only after defect 17 was fixed; together the two would have landed no diff on any arm.

nodes.label: Defect 19: mock deployments never exercise the streaming path
nodes.rationale: mock_response short-circuits inside anthropic_messages before litellm's streaming wrapper, so the success callback never fires for a streaming request -- and every real Claude Code call is streaming. Measured: two calls served, one captured. The gate now cross-checks its own capture against the proxy's access log.

nodes.label: Sonnet 5 tokenizer asymmetry in uniform token budgets
nodes.rationale: Sonnet 5's tokenizer produces ~30% more tokens for the same text, so a uniform output-token cap gives it ~30% less text budget than the other arms -- a config choice scored as a capability difference -- and cost-per-task is not directly comparable at equal text. Left to the calibration pilot, where cap derivation belongs.
